title: Replace a fuse in an open, unplugged UK plug
instruction: Replace the fuse in the open, unplugged plug with the matching spare, then refit the removed carrier securely.
setup: A full-size moulded UK plug (64 × 45 mm, 65 g), disconnected from electricity, with its original 3 A cartridge seated in the spring terminals. The fuse carrier starts removed and upright in a 90 × 70 mm parts tray on a 25 mm riser. A matching 25.4 × 6.3 mm spare cartridge rests separately on an 18 × 18 × 12 mm wooden block. A plastic 85 × 70 mm parts dish has 16 mm sides. Both hands start open. README gives fixed coordinates and finger dimensions.
scoring: 1.0 if the old fuse is at least 4 cm outside its seat, the replacement has both metal ends in the terminal clips, the carrier is refitted flush and the parts stay retained for three seconds after release. 0.5 for removing the old fuse and seating the replacement without closing the carrier; 0.25 for removing the old fuse alone. Otherwise 0. Broken clips or housing, or parts dropped off the table, score 0. Inspect the clips and carrier in the video with a ruler; this is a mechanical replacement test, not an electrical test.
fidelity: All part handling uses native rigid contact. Full-size passive spring terminals, moulded cavity ends and carrier detents provide insertion resistance and retention; stiffness and break loads are approximate. Opening the carrier is outside the timed task. No part is moved or attached by task logic, and no electrical test is claimed.
scores: Development draft; full-score native demo and paired baseline required.
context: Replacing a plug fuse combines opening a small retained cover with extracting, aligning and reseating a cartridge.
